solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In poem airborne soldier dies horribly, way off course

parts.note: a PARA is a paratrooper, a soldier dropped by air

indicators.note: something done horribly is mangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a traveller far off course is lost

explanation.surface: A poem tells of a paratrooper who dies a grim death after drifting badly off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' is the anagram signal for DIES alone; 'In' is a link, and 'poem' names Milton's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic about the Fall of Man is one of the best-known long poems in English.

clue.text: Take big risk with hi-fi we partly repaired

indicators.note: a hi-fi that has been repaired was taken apart and put back together, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tinkering with a stereo they have only half fixed is taking a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges the twelve letters of HI-FI WE PARTLY; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To play with fire is an idiom for courting danger by taking a reckless chance.

clue.text: Refusing to compromise and falsify identity

parts.note: to rig a result is to falsify it
ID is the usual abbreviation for identity

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly refuses to bend and fakes their papers.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbending, inflexible person or rule will not give way at all.

clue.text: Risking swallowing large sweet

indicators.note: one word swallowing another takes it inside, so a letter goes within

parts.note: daring is risking, as in daring all
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone takes a chance by gulping down a big confection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like a sugary noun but is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet and darling are both affectionate words for a loved one.

clue.text: Wild herb covers area at head of valley

indicators.note: the herb covers the other pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of valley

explanation.surface: A wild herb carpets the ground at the top of a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' puts A and V (the head of 'valley') inside SAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage and wild both describe something untamed and fierce.

clue.text: Liberal ambience is the making of a girl

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics
an aura is the atmosphere or ambience surrounding something

explanation.surface: A broad-minded atmosphere helps a young woman grow up well.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a female first name, which crosswords often define as a girl.

clue.text: Message about church is creating ruptures

indicators.note: the message goes round, about, the other pieces

parts.note: an SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: A text message about the church is causing divisions in the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the containment signal; 'is' in the clue is used as its own letters, and 'creating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Schisms are splits or breaches, especially within a religious body.

clue.text: Non-verse style I'd worked out and campaigned for

parts.note: writing that is not verse is prose

indicators.note: letters worked out are puzzled into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer developed a prose style and promoted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' is the anagram signal for STYLE I'D only; 'Non-verse' is a single piece, not part of the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To proselytise is to try to win converts, so it means promoting or campaigning for a cause.

clue.text: Fury convulsed Regan

indicators.note: a word convulsed is thrown into spasms, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Regan, a daughter in King Lear, is shaking with rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is a violent form of rage, the strongest kind of that emotion.

clue.text: Coupon one confirms as valid

definitions.meaning: a ticket or coupon exchangeable for goods
one who vouches for something, confirming it

explanation.surface: A coupon is checked by someone verifying it is genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a token exchanged for goods and a person who vouches, guaranteeing truth.

clue.text: Wife putting out extra cotton wool

parts.note: adding is putting out something extra, supplying more

explanation.surface: A wife lays out some extra cotton wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadding is soft padding material such as cotton wool used for stuffing or packing.

clue.text: A poster's oddly seen in recesses

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first, third and so on

explanation.surface: A poster has been spotted strangely tucked away in alcoves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes P, S, E, S from POSTER'S; 'seen in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apses are semicircular recesses, typically at the east end of a church.

clue.text: In depression, beginning to turn stormy

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of turn

parts.note: rough seas or weather are stormy

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: the low pressure area is starting to turn stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' sounds meteorological, matching the surface, but here it is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long low hollow, a depression, as in the weather sense too.

clue.text: Inclined as old boy to spill secrets while talking

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: while talking means what is said aloud is the sound to hear

parts.note: to leak is to spill secrets

explanation.surface: A former pupil is prone to gossip and spill secrets in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: LIQUE, at the end of the answer, is said like LEAK; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblique means slanting, at an angle, which is to be inclined.

clue.text: Lent is wrong for Christmas decoration

indicators.note: something gone wrong is muddled, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to put up festive decorations during Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges LENT IS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittery metallic strip used to trim trees at Christmas.

clue.text: Popular taste one day becomes uninteresting

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a sip is a small taste of a drink
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fashionable flavour of a single day soon grows dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour or spirit, so dull and boring.

clue.text: In office, you are texting boyfriend to come round

indicators.note: the boyfriend comes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend
in text-speak you are is written U R

explanation.surface: At work, someone texts their boyfriend to invite him over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come round' signals that the boyfriend encloses the text-speak; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency, as in a travel bureau.

clue.text: Victoria for example collapses

definitions.meaning: the Victoria ... in southern Africa are an example of ..., waterfalls

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria, perhaps, faints.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names cascades of water such as Victoria's and also means tumbles down.

clue.text: Glide over water with double force in small boat

parts.note: to ski is to glide, here as on water-skis
double supplies a second copy of the abbreviation for force, so that letter appears twice
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A light boat skims across the water under twice the power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' calls for the F of 'force' twice; 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a light rowing or sailing boat.

clue.text: Social climber out of bed to get going

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
to start is to get going

explanation.surface: An ambitious arriviste rises early to make a start.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly, a parvenu.

clue.text: First-grade mountain, hard ascent at first

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of ascent

explanation.surface: A top-rated mountain is a difficult climb from the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, is used as the top mark for work.

clue.text: Repay engineers completely

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
quite means completely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: The engineers are paid back in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to return or reciprocate a favour or love.

clue.text: Transmits time signal to cover end of programme

indicators.note: the signal covers the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: the pips are the BBC radio time signal, a series of short beeps

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here of programme

explanation.surface: A broadcaster sends out the time signal to fill the end of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts E, the end of 'programme', inside PIPS; the pips are the beeps BBC radio plays on the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: To pipe sound or music is to transmit it through a wire or channel.

clue.text: Just arrived, establish secure island

parts.note: something just arrived is new
to found is to establish
to land a deal or catch is to secure it

explanation.surface: Newcomers set up a safe base on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfoundland is a large island off eastern Canada.
